skill.name: when-validating-code-works-use-functionality-audit
skill.description: Validates generated or changed code by creating a sandbox, running realistic tests, debugging failures, and reporting production readiness.
skill.summary: Run execution-based functionality audits for generated or modified code.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, Graphviz labels, inline filenames, local test examples, and placeholder credentials. Confirmed risks involve temporary sandbox paths, persistence of full logs and reports, package installation, and Docker workspace mounts that require user review before execution.

remediation.issue: Unpinned package installation is recommended in setup and troubleshooting steps.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions, avoid global installs by default, and require explicit confirmation before any package install runs.

remediation.issue: Docker troubleshooting mounts the current workspace into a container.
remediation.suggestion: Use read-only mounts where possible, document the write risk, and prefer disposable copied workspaces for untrusted code.

remediation.issue: Full logs and reports are stored in Claude Flow memory.
remediation.suggestion: Store summaries by default and require redaction before persisting detailed logs or reports.

remediation.issue: Temporary sandbox paths use shared /tmp locations.
remediation.suggestion: Use unique, permission-restricted temporary directories and clean them only after confirming the exact target path.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Installation During Audit
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends global, project, and forced package installs during validation. Package installation can run lifecycle scripts and modify user environments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly install packages, including a global alpha package and a placeholder missing package. This is a clear supply-chain and environment-modification risk, though it is related to the skill purpose.

semantic_findings.title: Writable Docker Bind Mount of Workspace
semantic_findings.description: The Docker troubleshooting command mounts the current project directory into the container. A container process can write back into the workspace through this mount.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command uses a bind mount from the current directory to /workspace. The risk is contextual and not fully captured by the static command-substitution alert.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Storage of Test Logs and Reports
semantic_findings.description: The workflow stores full logs, reports, and metrics in Claude Flow memory. Test output can include credentials, stack traces, or proprietary code details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands persist complete logs and reports, not just summaries. Sensitive content depends on the project under test, so severity is medium rather than critical.

content.value_statement: Code can look complete while failing at runtime. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through sandboxed execution, debugging, and readiness reporting.
actual_capabilities: Creates an isolated audit workspace for running validation steps.
Runs tests with coverage and captures stdout, stderr, and exit codes.
Categorizes failures into syntax, runtime, logic, integration, and dependency issues.
Guides systematic fixes and reruns tests to detect regressions.
Produces audit reports, metrics, and production readiness checks.
limitations: Requires local tooling such as Node.js, Python, test frameworks, or Docker.
May install packages or run shell commands if the user follows examples directly.
Generated tests still need project-specific assertions and review.
Does not replace security review or manual product acceptance testing.

use_cases.title: Verify AI Generated Code
use_cases.description: Run generated code in a controlled environment before accepting it into a project.

use_cases.title: Check Pull Request Behavior
use_cases.description: Validate that changed modules still pass realistic tests and do not introduce regressions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Collect execution evidence, coverage status, and readiness signals before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation after a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the functionality audit skill to validate the changed code. Create a sandbox, run existing tests, and summarize failures with next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Validate One Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the authentication module for runtime correctness. Use realistic inputs, capture outputs, and report coverage and failing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Failing Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the functionality audit workflow on the failing test suite. Categorize root causes, propose minimal fixes, and rerun validation after changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build Release Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill as a release gate. Validate tests, coverage, regression status, and production readiness, then produce a concise go or no-go report.

output_examples.input: Validate the login flow after a refactor.
output: Login tests ran with coverage and two failures found.
Failures point to missing null checks and changed validation behavior.
Recommended next step is to fix validation and rerun regression tests.

output_examples.input: Check whether the data processor is ready for release.
output: All critical tests pass after one fix.
No regressions were detected in previously passing cases.
Release readiness is conditional on reviewing generated test assertions.

output_examples.input: Audit a new API endpoint before merging.
output: Endpoint tests cover success, authentication failure, and malformed input.
One integration mismatch was found in the response shape.
The report lists the failing behavior and the validation evidence needed after the fix.

best_practices: Run the workflow in a disposable sandbox with explicit user approval for installs.
Review generated tests before treating coverage or readiness metrics as final.
Redact secrets from logs and reports before storing or sharing audit artifacts.
anti_patterns: Do not run package installs or Docker commands blindly in a production workspace.
Do not accept passing tests when assertions only check trivial behavior.
Do not persist full logs when they may contain credentials or private data.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is designed around running tests and commands, so use a sandbox and review each command first.

faq.question: Can it prove that code is production ready?
faq.answer: It provides execution evidence and readiness checks, but final approval still needs human review and project-specific criteria.

faq.question: Does it create tests automatically?
faq.answer: It can generate starter tests, but those tests need meaningful assertions before they are trusted.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. The workflow can store logs and reports, so redact secrets and limit persistence.

faq.question: Can it run in CI?
faq.answer: Yes. The process includes CI examples, but package installs and artifact uploads should be reviewed first.
